brief: US equities closed the week/month down only modestly despite a sharp Friday selloff, as a bifurcating market saw AI-linked themes (Bitcoin Sensitive, Software, Agentic AI) underperform while Obesity Drugs, Defense, Biotech and Healthcare (XLV at a fresh high) outperformed on a defensive rotation out of TMT weakness. Semis fell ~8% Friday and the NDX posted its worst month since the AI cycle began, driven by mixed hyperscaler-era earnings (Kioxia, INTC guide-down, AMKR) and growing doubt about AI demand linearity beyond CY27, which is pressuring multiples. Hedge funds net bought equities for the first time in four weeks on short covers, but Info Tech and Mag 7 stayed net sold into month-end; Asset Managers finished net sellers. Russell 2000 outperformed on short-covering (open interest -$2.1bn) even as its CTA setup stays constrained by rate sensitivity; the S&P broke its medium-term CTA threshold (7544.2) Friday, and GS's momentum signal is set to flip negative if that holds, capping near-term upside. Ahead of Tuesday's midterms, GS recommends affordability- and policy-linked baskets (ACA beneficiaries long, drug-makers short, power-inflation longs, hyperscaler protection) since the options market is pricing a smaller move than Friday's actual S&P swing.
